extracted.intended_audience: students/scholars of literature and creative writers studying Aristotelian poetics
extracted.subtask_description: Applying Aristotle's aesthetic principles to composing and evaluating poetry (and related drama): emphasize imitation of the universal/ideal, internal causal probability, unity of form, and the artist's shaping/idealising activity rather than mere factual reportage or slavish copying of surface reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of sound and thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry is not merely the musical cadences or sound-effects of verse, nor is it only the ideas conveyed; both elements matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the extremes that reduce poetry to sound alone or to thought alone. Consider both the sonic qualities (cadence, musical effect) and the intellectual/contentual element when composing or evaluating verse. The text criticises the doctrine that 'poetry ... resides ... in the sound itself' as false and likewise warns against wholly ignoring musical effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation as expression of the universal (the ideal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Imitative art (poetry in its highest form) should be an expression of the universal element in human life: it discovers the 'form' (εἶδος) and reveals permanent and essential features rather than transient particulars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose/assess works by asking whether they render universal human types, motives, or forms—an idealised reality ('βέλτιον')—rather than merely reporting particulars. The aim is to bring out what is common and essential beneath individual facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate the accidental; idealise material
rubrics_metrics.description: Fine art 'eliminates what is transient and particular and reveals the permanent and essential'—the artist purifies reality of accidental detail to reveal form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adapting legend, history, or observation, strip away irrelevant or trivial detail and emphasize structural/essential elements. The artist 'stamps the given material with the impress of the form which is universal.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonise elements into an ideal unity
rubrics_metrics.description: The artist must harmonise selected elements into an ideal unity of type rather than merely selecting, combining, or embellishing without coherence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mere collage or decorative juxtaposition: the parts must be organised into a single, harmonious whole (an 'ideal unity'). The creative act is not servile copying but constructive synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority of internal causal coherence (probability/necessity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry should exhibit a more rigorous connexion of events: cause and event must be linked in 'probable or necessary sequence' (κατὰ τὸ εἰκὸς ἢ τὸ ἀναγκαῖον).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate plot and incident by internal logic and causal necessity within the work, not by whether incidents happen frequently in everyday life. The rule of probability pertains to the inner law that secures cohesion of parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters as embodiments of universal possibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Dramatic/poetic characters should represent universal possibilities (οἷα ἂν γένοιτο), not merely be average, commonplace people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create/assess characters capable of great deeds or passions whose actions follow the inner necessities of their type; their plausibility is judged by consistency with their dramatic role rather than statistical normality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom to represent what may happen rather than only what has happened
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry's distinguishing mark is that it relates 'what may happen' (the universal) rather than merely 'what has happened' (particular fact); the poet is not constrained to historical chronology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers may invent plausible but non-historical sequences and outcomes so long as they respect poetic/internal probability. Histories can be made into poetry by treating events as instances of the universal and arranging them with causal unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor factual/technical errors are tolerable if total impression remains
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors of fact or technical inaccuracy are not necessarily fatal provided they 'leave the total impression unimpaired.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging a work, weigh small inconsistencies or specialized errors less heavily if they do not undermine the overall truth, unity, or emotional effect of the piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic 'untruths' defended as higher truth (βέλτιον)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry may present things that are 'not real' in the empirical sense but are 'a higher reality'—the 'ought to be' (ὡς δεῖ), i.e., ideal truth that can surpass fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept imaginative departures from empirical truth when they serve to express deeper human or universal realities. Such departures should aim at the 'better' or the ideal rather than cheap fantasy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skillful fiction: maintain internal assumptions and avoid clashing with prosaic fact
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet must 'tell lies skilfully' (ψευδῆ λέγειν ὡς δεῖ) by making primary poetic assumptions and working consistently from them; the audience will accept the fiction if not dashed against prosaic reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When inventing marvellous or improbable premises, ensure the created world follows its own rules and that the narrative does not break the audience's willing suspension by conflicting with established facts of the work's own premises. This explains why Homerian marvels can be convincing within epic but would be problematic if they collide with mundane expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different tolerance for the marvellous in genres (epic vs drama)
rubrics_metrics.description: Epic admits marvellous and strange tales more freely than dramatic poetry, which requires tighter adherence to internal probability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose genre-appropriate degrees of invention: grand, marvellous episodes fit epic conventions; drama demands closer causal and psychological plausibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and transformation of traditional legend/history as raw material
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional legends and historical accounts are valuable sources but must be 'purified'—the poet must extract the poetic ore and idealize it before constructing a unified drama.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat historical or legendary material as starting material: remove the accidental and irrelevant, reshape episodes into a coherent plot that emphasizes essential, universal aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fine art's purpose differs from useful art: aim for ideal completion not practical function
rubrics_metrics.description: Fine art does not seek to modify the real world or serve practical needs; instead it completes nature by presenting a purified, ideal image of human life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When composing/evaluating art, judge whether it pursues an aesthetic end (revealing ideal form and human universals) rather than practical utility or mere technical workmanship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate poetic truth by inner artistic ends rather than empirical correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: The truth of poetry is different from factual truth: poetic truth is measured by the work's rendering of the universal and its internal artistic aims, not by literal correspondence with events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess a poem's truthfulness by its success in conveying the universal, its internal coherence, and its expressive power; allow departures from empirical fact when they illuminate deeper realities.
